title: Make release traceability lifecycle-aware and legacy-compatible
goal: Preserve strict release traceability without blocking the documented define-product to define-backlog sequence or brownfield legacy-grace migrations.
in_scope: Apply release completeness rollups only to releases already represented by at least one backlog epic
Begin full epic and story coverage enforcement as soon as a release is represented in the backlog
Downgrade legacy-attributable requirement rollup gaps to warnings while legacyContractGrace is active
Keep invalid or dangling prd_ref values and non-legacy validation failures blocking
Keep scripts/validate.mjs and the bootstrap scaffold copy behaviorally identical
out_of_scope: Automatically creating future-release epics or stories during define-product
Extending legacy grace to malformed coverage, status, dependency, or identifier contracts
Changing release_in_flight ownership or advancing it before define-backlog
acceptance: validate.mjs treats release traceability completeness as mandatory only after that release is represented in the backlog, so define-product may add future-release PRD requirements before define-backlog creates their epics; once represented, every requirement for that release must resolve through an epic and story, except that legacyContractGrace downgrades rollup gaps caused by historical stories without prd_ref to warnings while dangling references and all non-legacy contract errors still fail.
invariants: An unrepresented future PRD release does not invalidate the current backlog
Adding the first epic for a release activates completeness checks for that release
Legacy grace never authorizes invented requirement identifiers or malformed contract data
Current release traceability remains complete and mechanically verifiable
